# Redistributable local pipeline fixtures

These files are intentionally included by .gitignore. JPEGs have been EXIF-oriented,
resized to at most 1280px and re-encoded without metadata. Used for software testing,
not endorsements. No owner camera images belong here.

| File | Source / author | License | Expected visible content |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.jpg | [Batman and Waluigi](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Batman_and_Waluigi.jpg), Sahaib | [CC BY 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) | Two partial people, Batman mask and Waluigi hat; difficult selfie overlap |
| 1.jpg | [Halloween in Iraq](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Flickr_-_The_U.S._Army_-_Halloween_in_Iraq.jpg), Sgt. 1st Class Daniel Ewer / Task Force 34, US Army | US federal public domain | Group: Ghostbuster, reflective wrapped suit, ambiguous white-shirt costume, Cat in the Hat; ordinary black-shirt bystander; dim indoor scene |
| 2.jpg | [Europe District Halloween](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Europe_District_celebrates_Halloween_(8141670465).jpg), US Army Corps of Engineers Europe District | US federal public domain | Owl costume, sunglasses/beak, feathered vest |
| 3.jpg | [Inflatable costume](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Inflatable_costume.jpg), Eli Christman | [CC BY 2.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/2.0/) | Inflatable deer suit at a party |
| 4.jpg | [Big Little Witch](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Big_Little_Witch_(178809389).jpeg), Nicu Buculei | [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0/) | Held-out witch costume; resized derivative remains CC BY-SA 3.0 |

Not an accuracy benchmark representative of all doorbells. Real photographs include
occlusion, background people and unusual costumes; report detection misses as well
as classification errors. Confidence is uncalibrated model output, not probability.

Source licenses checked on October 25, 2026. Copyright licenses do not imply subject consent or endorsement; no model releases are supplied. These files are for reproducible software tests, not identity recognition.
